Race: Member of the State Assembly — AD-17 (California State Assembly), November 3, 2026 general election.
Our research selects Matt Haney as the strongest candidate in this race.

RECOMMENDED CANDIDATE: Matt Haney (D)
- Our assessment: Haney called Israel's actions in Gaza a genocide in a 2026 CAIR-SFBA Liberty Award recording and invited Gaza children through HEAL Palestine to speak on the State Assembly floor. CAIR Action endorsed him and Vote for Peace rated him Ally. Those actions sit alongside his aye vote on AB 715, which creates an antisemitism coordinator and classroom-material oversight in California schools, and Strong Support from California Jewish Democrats, the renamed Demo…
- Record (2026-02-23): Haney invited HEAL Palestine's Global Healing children from Gaza to the California State Assembly floor in Sacramento to speak about their treatment.
- Record (2025-09-13): CalMatters lists Matt Haney as recorded Aye on AB 715 (Assembly Floor). The bill creates an antisemitism coordinator and classroom-material oversight; its text does not explicitly name IHRA.
- Record (2023-08-28): Haney voted aye on SB 403 (caste bill) in Assembly Judiciary and on final Assembly passage 2023-08-28, retaining the word caste.
- Record (2026-10-23): Haney publicly called Israel’s actions in Gaza a genocide in CAIR-SFBA’s 2026 Liberty Award recording. The owner confirmed this statement in the linked video.
- Muslim-community / pro-Palestine-aligned records: CAIR Action (endorsed); AROC Action (endorsed)

No other candidate in this race has a researched record.

Write ONE voter-facing paragraph of up to 200 words explaining why a voter should support Matt Haney in this race and why Matt Haney is stronger than the other candidates above, grounded in the textual records shown. OUR FRAMEWORK: voters judge candidates first on two litmus tests — opposing the genocide in Gaza and ending U.S. military/economic aid to Israel. When the recommended candidate's shown record contains concrete acts on these tests (cosponsoring the Block the Bombs Act, voting against arms funding, calling it a genocide, divestment action), name the specific acts with their dates or bill names as shown. When the shown record does NOT contain them, be transparent: one plain sentence stating what the candidate has not done on the record (for example: has not called it a genocide; has not backed blocking weapons transfers; voted for aid bills), then explain why the candidate is still the best option listed. Never hide a shortfall and never invent one. Do not write meta-language like 'the record does not show' or 'has not published a stated position' — write about what the candidate has or has not done. A candidate who refused to properly support Palestinians when put in the position (a contrary vote, an opposed resolution, rejecting community asks) gets that held against them; an abstention under heavy pressure can read as qualified support if the shown assessment says so — follow the shown assessments.  Rules: never mention any numeric score or rating; a letter grade may appear at most in passing — prefer explaining actual acts, votes, statements and positions. Use ONLY the facts shown; never add outside knowledge or invent events, dates, quotes or endorsements; if a competitor has no shown record, say nothing about them. Endorsements: mention only the 'Muslim-community / pro-Palestine-aligned records' and 'Israel-aligned / AIPAC / Hindu-nationalist-aligned records' lines (Muslim-aligned backing supports a candidate; AIPAC/UDP/DMFI/ICAN or Hindu-nationalist-aligned backing or opposition is a relevant contrast); never name any other endorser. Plain prose, no lists, no quotation marks, no headings, no AI disclaimer. Name the office once. Output ONLY the paragraph.

Samir Laymoun source policy: omit his support, opposition and comments from voter prose when other relevant directional evidence exists. Do not retain his opinion anonymously as 'an activist' or 'a personal guide'. Exceptions: the Kamal Yassin race, or a candidate for whom his opinion is the only relevant directional evidence. Check the complete current research, not just an old summary. Where allowed, state the support/opposition or relevant comment briefly and accurately. Never relabel his opinion as BAMC Action's position or as the candidate's own policy. Never explain that he is an individual rather than an institution, an activist opinion source, owner-requested, or separate from official organizational positions. Those classifications belong in the audit, not the voter paragraph. Preserve genuinely material facts and qualifications; do not turn a tactical recommendation into agreement on policy.

FACTUAL CORRECTIONS: October 23, 2026 is only the video's upload date. Do not state that Haney spoke on that date; say the recording was uploaded then, or omit that date. The AB 715 vote complicates his Palestine record under our rubric; do not portray it as a positive Palestinian-justice action or as a reason to praise him. Do not fault a state Assembly member for not casting congressional arms-transfer or military-aid votes. Do not invent unrecorded positions or claim his unresearched opponent is worse. Preserve his genocide statement, HEAL Palestine action, relevant endorsements and the material AB 715 concern. Output one voter-facing paragraph, up to 200 words, no methodology or missing-record disclaimer padding.
